Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team started the vendor review and has a few open items specific to data residency and private deployment controls before we move onto procurement:

1) Explicit confirmation of which AWS regions Redwood will host Veridian Health production workloads in for the initial rollout (EU primary, APAC failover) and whether backups are stored outside those regions.
2) A short description of the VPC/network topology for Private deployments (VPCs, peering, Transit Gateway usage, PrivateLink, egress controls).
3) Evidence artifacts: network diagram (redacted ok), SOC 2 scope excerpt showing that hosting regions are included, and a VPC config export or sample security group/route tables.

Timeline: our compliance review is aiming to close by Dec 10 — would you be able to provide the artifacts by EOD Dec 5?

If you prefer, send a short attestation statement we can include in the SIG/CAIQ responses and we'll treat the attachments as supporting evidence.

Best,
Liam

Hi all,

Attaching the VPC config export (vpc_config_export.json) and a very brief technical summary below:

- VPC topology: each customer Private deployment uses a dedicated VPC per region (no multi-tenant peering). For multi-region customers we provision one VPC in EU (eu-west-1) and one in APAC (ap-southeast-1) when requested.
- Connectivity: options supported — AWS PrivateLink endpoints for control-plane APIs, Transit Gateway for large-scale inter-VPC routing, and customer-managed VPC peering where required.
- Ingress/Egress controls: default deny at security group layer, explicit egress whitelists for patching/outbound monitoring endpoints, and NAT Gateway usage only for controlled egress subnets.
- KMS & encryption: customer keys (BYOK) are supported and mapped to regional KMS keys per deployed region. Data at rest uses AES-256 and TLS1.2+ for transit.
- Backups: snapshot lifecycle runs in-region by default; cross-region snapshot replication is implemented only when enabled in the customer's deployment configuration and documented in the SOW.

Note: sensitive route table IDs and exact IP ranges redacted in the export. If Veridian needs live cloud logs (CloudTrail/Flow logs) we can provide time-limited access to a read-only S3 bucket or a shared logging account export.

-Michael
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- vpc_config_export.json (export with redacted identifiers)

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple clarifications before we close:

1) For the APAC failover — can you confirm whether the failover is cold (manual promotion) or warm (replicated, RPO/RTO targets)? We need this to populate our risk worksheet.
2) For backups: please confirm retention windows and whether encryption keys for backups are colocated in the same regional KMS keys you referenced.

Also, if you can provide a one-paragraph signed attestation that the deployment for Veridian Health will keep production and backups in-region (EU) unless we explicitly authorize cross-region replication, that would expedite our SIG completion. The unsigned paragraph in Evelyn's note is fine for now, but Security would prefer signature on company letterhead for the final record.

Best,
Liam
